description: I am an AI and Data Science student passionate about solving real-world challenges using technology. I have experience in machine learning, computer vision, deep learning, and full-stack development, with projects using YOLOv8, MiDaS, and RAG. I look forward to exploring NASA’s open data and building innovative solutions with teammates skilled in data science, web development, UI/UX, astronomy, or geospatial analysis.
summary:
Selecting future lunar bases and Mars landing sites requires testing equipment in terrestrial analogs; however, traditional site selection relies on visual approximations and overlooks physical differences. We developed TerraTwin, a multi-scale computational planetary analog discovery engine that moves beyond visual similarity by evaluating sites across 8 quantitative geophysical dimensions derived from open NASA, CSA, ESA, and JAXA datasets.

TerraTwin characterizes 8 flagship planetary targets (including Artemis III Shackleton Crater, Marius Hills lava tubes, and Mars Jezero Crater) against 10 global Earth analogs spanning 6 continents and subterranean volcanic cavities. To overcome single-site physical limits, TerraTwin introduces algorithmic Dual-Site Campaign Synthesis (combining sites to achieve >92% exploration coverage) alongside deterministic hardware protocols for Bekker wheel sinkage, rover mechanical gravity offloading, and optical solar attenuation. The system features a responsive Next.js mission workbench, live NASA CMR API querying, and an unsupervised 2D PCA latent space explorer.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

TerraTwin is a full-stack planetary analog characterization system combining an interactive web workbench with automated scientific data pipelines:

  • 8D Calibrated Vector Characterization: Every planetary target and Earth analog is mapped to an 8-dimensional normalized feature vector (v∈[0,100]8\mathbf{v} \in [0, 100]^8v∈[0,100]8) covering: Geology/Mineralogy, Topography/SAR Roughness, Thermal/Insolation, Cryogenic Volatiles/ISRU, Aeolian Dynamics, Astrobiology/Extremophiles, Subsurface Cavities, and Terramechanics/Mobility.
  • Hybrid Similarity Scoring Engine: Uses a calibrated Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel combined with Cosine directional alignment (SFinal=0.55⋅SRBF+0.45⋅SCosine−δS_{\text{Final}} = 0.55 \cdot S_{\text{RBF}} + 0.45 \cdot S_{\text{Cosine}} - \deltaSFinal​=0.55⋅SRBF​+0.45⋅SCosine​−δ), preventing artificial score clustering and yielding a realistic 75%–96% match spread.
  • Unsupervised 2D Latent Space (PCA & K-Means): Projects multi-agency planetary dimensions into a 2D coordinate plane capturing 61.7% of total variance, automatically categorizing sites into 4 geophysical archetypes: Lacustrine/Sulfate Basins, Cryogenic Polar Traps, Basaltic Impact Rims, and Subterranean Lava Cavities.
  • Dual-Site Campaign Synthesis: Recognizes that no single Earth site replicates all conditions, automatically pairing complementary micro-sites (e.g., pairing lunar highland calcic anorthosite with high-Arctic permafrost polygons) to reach >92% exploration envelope fidelity.
  • Operational Hardware Protocols: Computes Bekker terramechanic wheel sinkage (z0z_0z0​) under lunar and Martian gravity, specifies rover counterweight offloading in Newtons, and calculates neutral-density optical attenuation filters for testing planetary cameras under terrestrial sunlight.
  • In-Browser Custom Outcrop Scanner: Enables field scientists to input custom GPS coordinates, slope, radar backscatter, and temperature to project uncharted field sites live into the PCA latent space.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates Visual Confirmation Bias: Replaces "looks like Mars" intuition with calibrated radar decibels (σ0\sigma^0σ0), Sentinel-2 SWIR mineral ratios, and thermal inertia (PPP).
  • Tactical Micro-Site Precision: Targets sub-kilometer zones (e.g., ejecta blankets and volcanic skylights) rather than over-generalized geographic regions.
  • Risk Mitigation & Cost Reduction: Helps flight teams verify robotics, mobility, and scientific instruments under mathematically modeled boundary conditions before mission deployment, preventing multimillion-dollar hardware failures.
  • Comprehensive Failure Analysis: Explicitly outlines both "Why This Analog Works" and "Where It Breaks Down & Constraints" for every location.

3. What is the intended impact?

TerraTwin directly assists mission planners, roboticists, and planetary scientists designing hardware and astronaut protocols for NASA's Artemis III lunar south pole expeditions, long-duration lunar base infrastructure, and future human Mars landing missions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend Workbench: Next.js 14, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React icons, and dynamic SVG rendering for the 8-axis radar profiles and 2D PCA latent space.
    • nasa_earthdata_fetcher.py: Automated, zero-key HTTP client connecting to NASA's EOSDIS Common Metadata Repository (CMR) API.
    • sar_backscatter_calculator.py: Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Rayleigh roughness & LRO Mini-RF Circular Polarization Ratio (CPR) processor.
    • cli_analog_finder.py: Terminal-based analog discovery CLI with mission hardware weighting presets.
  • GIS & Mapping: Embedded Google Maps Satellite Viewport, NASA Moon Trek GIS, and NASA Mars Trek GIS integrations.

5. How is your project creative?

TerraTwin solves the fundamental challenge of planetary analog science: the single-site paradox. Instead of forcing a single Earth location to act as an impossible 100% twin, TerraTwin creatively synthesizes dual-site mission campaigns. Furthermore, it embeds real-time mathematical Bekker terramechanics and mechanical gravity compensation into the interface, transforming analog scouting into an active engineering test simulator.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team implemented solutions for all 11 Official NASA Space Apps Challenge Considerations:

  1. Beyond visual similarity: Integrated radar backscatter (σ0\sigma^0σ0), SWIR mineralogy, and thermal inertia.
  2. Multiple dimensions: Exact 1-to-1 parity with NASA’s 8 physical dimensions.
  3. Strengths & breakdowns: Dual cards for every site detailing operational limits.
  4. Geological processes: Dedicated process twins (e.g., cryoturbation, impact shock metamorphism, lava tube inflation).
  5. Beyond well-known sites: Uncovered uncharted gems (Rogaland anorthosite, Lonar basalt rim, Dallol acid delta, Umm Jirsan tube) alongside benchmarks.
  6. Whole Earth & subsurface: Explored 6 continents plus subterranean lava conduits.
  7. Multi-agency data: Synthesized data across NASA, CSA, ESA, and JAXA.
  8. Scale: Micro-scale resolution (<1 km2<1 \text{ km}^2<1 km2 grids) with tactical coordinates.
  9. Exploration connection: Bekker wheel sinkage, rover counterweights, and solar flux filters.
  10. Earth's physical limits: Quantified gravity offload percentages (Luna 83.5%, Mars 62.2%) and vacuum chamber requirements.
  11. Surprise factor: Interactive in-browser PCA latent space and dual-site synergy pairing.
